report.summary: Chunk 6 of gated_writes.py: defines _read_gitdir_pointer (safety-critical), _PinnedWorktreeGit class, _reattempt function, and _as_cancel_predicate helper.
risks: _PinnedWorktreeGit.__init__ | high | Captures admin_dir once; if worktree .git pointer is already compromised before construction, pinning does not help. | Verify construction always precedes first git apply in callers.
_PinnedWorktreeGit.run | medium | Raises RuntimeError on non-zero exit; caller may not catch it, leaking candidate state. | Audit callers for exception handling.
_reattempt | medium | Imports run_attempt from daedalus.spine.attempt; if that module changes signature, this breaks silently. | Add integration tests for reattempt path.
_as_cancel_predicate | low | Swallows all exceptions from callable cancel; may hide programming errors. | Consider logging swallowed exceptions.
todos: Verify that _read_gitdir_pointer is called before any git apply in every code path.
Add unit tests for _as_cancel_predicate with various cancel token types.

symbols.name: _read_gitdir_pointer
symbols.note: Reads .git file/directory from worktree; returns Path or None.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit
symbols.note: Captures admin_dir once; runs git commands pinned to that dir.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes with worktree path and reads admin_dir.

symbols.name: _PinnedWorktreeGit.run
symbols.note: Executes git subprocess with pinned --git-dir and --work-tree.

symbols.name: _reattempt
symbols.note: Re-runs TaskAttempt for a candidate with a new base revision.

symbols.note: Normalises cancel token to a zero-arg predicate.

claims.text: Every git call against ONE worktree, pinned to the admin dir read BEFORE any candidate-authored patch is applied into it.
claims.why: The class captures admin_dir in __init__ (before any apply), and run() uses that captured path via --git-dir and --work-tree.

claims.text: Mirrors daedalus.spine.attempt's _read_gitdir_pointer + _git(..., git_dir=, work_tree=) pattern (independently written here; both are module-private there).
claims.why: The referenced module daedalus.spine.attempt is not in this chunk; cannot verify mirroring.

claims.text: a linked worktree's .git is a FILE containing gitdir: <path>.
claims.why: _read_gitdir_pointer reads the .git file and handles the 'gitdir:' prefix.

claims.text: the pointer is read ONCE, at construction -- callers must construct this immediately after create_worktree and before the first git apply
claims.why: admin_dir is read in __init__ and stored; subsequent calls to run() use the stored value.

claims.text: every subsequent call is pinned to that captured path explicitly, never re-resolved from the (by-then possibly candidate-controlled) working tree.
claims.why: run() always uses self.admin_dir and self.worktree from construction.

claims.text: Re-run the SAME instruction/target_paths against a NEW base commit.
claims.why: It creates a fresh_spec with new base_revision but same content (via _dc_replace).

claims.text: Used only when the integration branch has moved past the base a candidate's artifact was built against -- see promote_candidates.
claims.why: promote_candidates is not in this chunk; cannot verify usage.

claims.text: A fresh TaskSpec (same content, new base_revision) through the same TaskAttempt/offload_runner path as Phase 1: no new isolation mechanism, just the existing one invoked again with an updated base.
claims.why: It calls run_attempt with fresh_spec and a runner/gate setup similar to Phase 1.

claims.text: cancel is forwarded unchanged to this regeneration's own TaskAttempt
claims.why: cancel parameter is passed to run_attempt as cancel=cancel.

claims.text: Normalise a cancel token to a zero-arg predicate, for the ONE call site in this module (the cumulative re-gate's RunnerContext.is_cancelled, see _promote_one_inner) that builds a RunnerContext directly rather than going through TaskAttempt (which does this normalisation itself, internally, for every cancel this module forwards via run_attempt).
claims.why: References to _promote_one_inner and RunnerContext are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT an import of daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate -- that name is module-private there, and this file's own convention is to mirror a small private helper rather than reach across another module's underscore boundary (see _read_gitdir_pointer above, which does the same for the same reason).
claims.why: The function is defined locally, not imported. Also _read_gitdir_pointer is defined locally in this chunk.

claims.text: Same three-way contract as the original: None -> never cancelled; a callable -> called, a broken callable treated as 'not cancelled' (a token that raises must not be able to abort work it was only supposed to observe); anything exposing is_set() (a threading.Event, a KillSwitch) -> that, same broken-token rule.
claims.why: The code handles None (returns lambda: False), callable (calls it, catches exceptions returning False), and checks hasattr 'is_set' (implied by the else branch; the else branch does not check for is_set but the docstring claims it does; however, the code shown does not include that branch; verdict is kept because the docstring describes intended behavior but the code may be incomplete in this chunk; actually the chunk ends after the callable branch, so the is_set branch is not shown; verdict should be uncheckable because the branch is not present. Wait: the chunk ends at 'return _call' after the callable branch. The else branch (for is_set) is not shown. So the claim about 'anything exposing is_set' is not verifiable in this chunk. Verdict: uncheckable.

observations.what: _read_gitdir_pointer returns None if .git is a directory; _PinnedWorktreeGit.run() handles admin_dir=None by not adding --git-dir and --work-tree flags.
_as_cancel_predicate's docstring claims it handles objects with is_set() method, but the code shown in this chunk only handles None and callable; the is_set branch is missing.
_reattempt uses _recording_runner and gate functions that are not defined in this chunk; they are assumed to be available.
